title: 2026-10-22_Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_3a4
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux/Remaiten botnet incident on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation in the local sandbox.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external server? Submit the service name.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services related to network communication or external connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to check the status of the suspicious service.

levels.title: Identify Flood Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating the flood of network traffic? Submit the service name.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service is named `bot-flood.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with names or descriptions related to network traffic or flooding.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to check the status of the flood service.

levels.title: Identify Timer Service
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the timer service that ensures the suspicious service starts automatically after reboot? Submit the timer service name.
levels.solution: Look for timer services in the systemd configuration that might be related to the suspicious service. The timer service is named `bot-beacon.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for timer services in the systemd configuration that might be related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd timers and look for any timers associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.timer` to check the status of the timer service.
